#### Utilities

```{r}
plot_logo <- function(df, read_one = TRUE){
  # If it's read two, let's reverse it for readability
  if (!read_one){
    df$x <- unlist(lapply(df$x, FUN = function(x) intToUtf8(rev(utf8ToInt(x)))))
  }
  
  df$first_hundred <- substr(df$x, 1, 100)
  df$next_hundred <- substr(df$x, 101, 200)
  df$last_bases <- substr(df$x, 200, 251)
  
  # Why are some going negative?
  pmw_max_one <- pmax(PWM(DNAStringSet(df$first_hundred)), 0.00)
  pmw_max_two <- pmax(PWM(DNAStringSet(df$next_hundred)), 0.00)
  pmw_max_three <- pmax(PWM(DNAStringSet(df$last_bases)), 0.00)
  
  p1 <- ggseqlogo(pmw_max_one) + xlab("Position") + scale_x_continuous(breaks=1:100, labels=1:100) + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1))
  
  p2 <- ggseqlogo(pmw_max_two) + xlab("Position") + scale_x_continuous(breaks=1:100, labels=101:200) + theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1))
  
  p3 <- ggseqlogo(pmw_max_three) + xlab("Position") + scale_x_continuous(breaks=1:51, labels=201:251)+ theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1))
  
  tmp <- ggarrange(p1, p2, ggarrange(p3, ncol = 2, nrow = 1), 
                   ncol = 1, nrow = 3, common.legend = TRUE, legend = "bottom")
  
  return(tmp)
}
```

## UMI annotation and masking of primer regions

Next, the score subcommand of `MaskPrimers.py` is used to identify and remove the PCR primers for both reads. When dealing with Ig sequences, it is important to cut or mask the primers, as B cell receptors are subject to somatic hypermutation (the accumulation of point mutations in the DNA) and degenerate primer matches can look like mutations in downstream applications. The MaskPrimers tool is also used to annotate each read 1 sequence with the 15 nucleotide UMI that precedes the C-region primer (`MaskPrimers score --barcode`):


**Note:** The BARCODE exists as ten base pairs immediately after the reverse complement of the read one primer (Primer: "TCGTCGGCAGCGTCAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAG", RevCom: "CTGTCTCTTATACACATCTGACGCTGCCGACGA"), WHICH IS FOUND ON READ 2!

**Note:** We will mask the first primers, and cut the second ones.

```
docker run -v /Users/emoseley/VHH/data:/data immcantation/suite:4.4.0 \
  MaskPrimers.py score -s /data/MS12_R1_quality-pass.fastq -p /data/strictAlpVHH_R2_12Nov23.fasta \
      --start 0 --mode mask --outname R1 --log  /data/MP1.log
```

Note: we use `--start 10` because the `--barcode` is length 10 and precedes the primer region. _However_, it looks like the barcode is picking up information on the opposite side of the read...

      --start 10 --barcode --mode cut --maxerror 0.5 \
      --outname R2 --log /data/MP2.log

## Generating Consensus Sequences

In this task, a single consensus sequence is constructed for each set of reads annotated with the same UMI barcode. As the UMI barcode is part of read 1, the `BARCODE` annotation identified by `MaskPrimers.py` must first be copied to the read 2 mate-pair of each read 1 sequence. 

Propogation of annotations between mate pairs is performed using `PairSeq.py` which also removes unpaired reads and ensures that paired reads are sorted in the same order across files:





















```{bash}
docker run -v /Users/emoseley/VHH/data:/data immcantation/suite:4.4.0 \
  AssemblePairs.py align -1 /data/A2A_S1_L001_R2_001.fastq -2 /data/A2A_S1_L001_R1_001.fastq \
    --coord illumina --rc tail --maxerror 0.1 --outname ALPACA1 --log /data/ALPACA_AP.log 
```
